newsitem.title: USA: Genelabs trial does not show significance.
newsitem.headline: Genelabs trial does not show significance.

text.p: Genelabs Technologies Inc said on Friday a treatment response to its GL701 was observed in a group of women with clinically active systemic lupus erythematosus, but the study did not achieve statistical significance when all patients were included.
The group of women which showed a response constituted the majority of patients enrolled in the company's first pivotal clinical trial for GL701, Genelabs said.
When all patients were included, an unexpectedly high response rate to placebo was observed among patients with minimal or no disease activity at baseline, Genelabs said.

The Phase III trial was designed to show whether the use of GL701 in women with systemic lupus erythematosus would allow reduction in their steroid doses while maintaining stable or reduced disease activity, the company said.

GL701, Genelabs' compound, is a pharmaceutical preparation that contains dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) as the active ingredient, it said. DHEA is a naturally occurring hormone that is produced by the adrenal glands, it said.
Further detailed analysis of the study is continuing, which will be discussed with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Genelabs said.
It said it will work very closely with the FDA regarding GL701's clinical development program going forward.
A second Phase III study to evaluate the use of GL701 for systemic lupus erythematosus, using a different design and clinical endpoints, is ongoing, the company said.

That trial, which the company started in March 1996, is designed to determine if GL701 could improve clinical outcome or disease symptoms in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, Genelabs said. The company said it anticipated 300 women with systemic lupus erythematosus would receive either GL701 or placebo for 12 months for that trial.

In the first Phase III trial, preliminary analysis of patients stratified by baseline disease activity indicates a positive trend favoring GL701 over placebo for patients with active disease, it said.

In the trial, 191 women with mild to moderate systemic lupus, who were receiving daily doses of 10-30 mg of prednisone, were enrolled in the double-blind, placebo- controlled trial in 18 sites in the United States, it said.
Patients received either placebo or 100 mg or 200 mg of GL701 daily for seven to nine months, it said.
At enrollment, baseline disease activity index scores ranged from zero to 22, with zero indicating absence of recent disease activity, with a median of four, Genelabs said.
During the study, steroid doses were reduced at each visit according to the study protocol, provided a patient's disease activity score had not increased, Genelabs said.

Among patients with baseline disease activity scores greater than two, about 72 percent of total patients, it said a clinically meaningful difference in the percent who achieved a sustained reduction of steroids to physiological levels was observed between the 200 mg dose and placebo groups.
No such difference between treatment groups was observed among patients with baseline disease activity scores of two or or less, Genelabs said.

Preliminary results also indicated that GL701 was well tolerated in women with systemic lupus. But it said safety results could not be extrapolated to the general population because patients with systemic lupus are believed to have abnormally low DHEA levels.

This Phase III study, the first multi-center, placebo-controlled clinical trial for a new investigational compound for systemic lupus in more than 30 years, suggested a daily administration of 200 mg of GL701 allowed reduction of steroid doses in those women with active disease, it said.
Many systemic lupus patients depend heavily on steroids such as prednisone to control their disease, it said.

Genelabs said the study also suggested that women with low disease activity, or with scores between zero and two, might be able to reduce their steroid usage, as no difference in the percentage of responders was observed between the placebo and GL701 treatment groups for women with low disease activity.
